solution.what: WAINUT contribution: located catalogue 653 on NARA M97 roll 10 frames 0298-0303 (Ellis, Mexico, 16 Nov 1839), in the JQA code (the = 1385), with the Department's clear copy on frames 0300-0301.

WAINUT contribution: applied ../jqa/code_table.tsv unchanged: 471 of 519 groups valued; joined into letters, the table-only decode recovers 88% of the clear copy's letters (difflib ratio 0.868; shuffled tables 0.12-0.22, shuffled group orders 0.20-0.22).

WAINUT contribution: groups aligned line by line with the 1839 clear copy (ellis1839_pairs.tsv, about 40 pairs): 1261 comma, 1264 full stop (the table has gar, H, 1x), 1067 s, 651 x, 1366 tal, 601 713 Mr.; the copy's 'Toops' repeats the groups' spelling.
WAINUT contribution: wrong-key controls (decode.py --controls): function-word rate 0.28 for the true table, 0.02-0.12 for shifts of 1-100, 0.03 for random table permutations.
WAINUT contribution: Manning, Inter-American Affairs vol. 8 (1937) not reachable (bot check, not bypassed); two web searches found no printed text.
WAINUT contribution: read (ellis1839_reading.md, read_share 1.0), following the groups where they differ from the clear copy.

outcome.method_basis: Every coded passage of 1836-39 has a contemporary decipherment: filmed with the despatches (the Department's clean copies, clear copies or interlinear clear; for 1839 the clear copy on vol. 9 frames 0300-0301), or for 26 Oct 1836 in print (Bosch García 1984). texts.label: Ellis to Forsyth, Mexico, 26 Oct 1836, coded close (catalogue 653), M97 roll 8 frames 0323-0324
texts.summary: The Mexican officers are confident of the coming campaign against Texas, but panic already runs through the soldiers, and government and people are disappointed because news from England leaves them no hope of help from that power.
texts.note: The one coded passage with no decipherment on the film; text printed by Bosch García 1984. Three closing groups found on frame 0324.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the decode line by line and against Bosch Garcia's printed text; agrees except the groups' extra "but"; 285 left open, 1114 marked [?].

texts.label: Ellis to Forsyth, No. 9, Mexico, 16 Nov 1839 (catalogue 653), M97 roll 10 frames 0298-0303
texts.summary: The US minister in Mexico reports that Texian troops with disaffected Mexicans have crossed the line, apparently to attack Matamoros, and that the government is sending General Arista to the frontier with 4,000 men; a war with Texas would unite the Mexican parties; the foreign minister Cañedo wants a general congress of the Spanish American states, unlikely to succeed. The Department's 1839 clear copy is in the same file.
texts.note: A contemporary decipherment exists (prior solution, used); this entry adds the groups, the decode with the table and the alignment. reading_review left to the maintainer.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the decryption and the 1839 clear copy after the 14 disputed groups were settled on the frames; every group lines up with the copy.

outcome.notes: Catalogue 653, merged 27 Oct 2026: Brackx's 1836-40 material (issue #120) and WAINUT's No. 9 of 1839 (PR #107). Same code as ../jqa; nothing there is changed. Ellis values are an overlay (ellis1839_pairs.tsv; Brackx's ellis_values.tsv in his gist), not edits to the table. The 1836 passages other than 26 Oct are read from the decipherments on the film and in Bosch Garcia; their group transcriptions are in Brackx's gist, so they have no outcome.texts entry here. The other 1836-37 despatches (about 3,600 groups on M97 rolls 8-9, Brackx) are left out of documents until his files are in the repository.
